reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents an ordinary retail savings promotion offering a $25 Target gift card for purchasing at least $100 of specified baby products, alongside additional coupons. The requested action is a qualifying purchase and coupon use rather than providing an investment, payment to an unknown party, credentials, or other sensitive information. The historical offer's activation or fulfillment is not established.

citations.quote: EARN A FREE $25 GIFT CARD WITH BABY PURCHASE (Starting 9/27)
offering up a FREE $25 Gift Card when you purchase $100 worth of Diapers, Training Pants, Baby Wipes and/or Formula!
check out all of the great coupons that you can stack to sweeten things even further
Click HERE - http://hip2save.com/2015/09/24/target-free-25-gift-card-w-100-purchase-of-select-baby-products-starting-927/

opening.argument: The message ties a concrete $25 reward directly to viewer action: the title says viewers can earn it with a baby purchase, while the description conditions it on buying $100 of specified products. It then adds a second participation path by directing viewers to click an external link for coupons. That is a solicitation built around a promised reward, not merely discussion of shopping. The appeal depends on viewers spending money first and following the promoted link to maximize the promised benefit, while the supplied material does not establish the reward's actual fulfillment.

citations.quote: EARN A FREE $25 GIFT CARD WITH BABY PURCHASE (Starting 9/27)
offering up a FREE $25 Gift Card when you purchase $100 worth of Diapers, Training Pants, Baby Wipes and/or Formula!
Be sure to watch the video and click the link below to check out all of the great coupons that you can stack to sweeten things even further

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the purchase a qualification does not remove the solicitation: the reward is the reason viewers are encouraged to spend $100, and the external link is presented as a way to improve the payoff. The cited offer language describes what viewers are supposed to do, but it does not establish that the gift card was actually issued or that the linked coupon path was reliable. A retail setting can still be used to induce action through an unverified reward claim.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted material shows a conditional store promotion, not a low-barrier giveaway: the viewer must buy specified baby products, and the description identifies an ordinary $100 purchase threshold. Nothing shows payment to an unknown party, credential collection, or a promise of money for doing nothing. The fact that fulfillment is not independently established is uncertainty, not evidence that the promotion is deceptive.

EARN A FREE $25 GIFT CARD WITH BABY PURCHASE (Starting 9/27)

opening.argument: Several pressure signals reinforce one another. The offer is framed as a free $25 gift card, but only after a substantial $100 purchase, and it is introduced as starting tomorrow, creating time pressure. Viewers are also urged to click an external website and stack additional coupons, expanding the action beyond the advertised purchase. The supplied evidence presents the attractive reward and urgency prominently, but does not provide complete terms or proof of fulfillment. That combination can make an ordinary-looking offer persuasive while leaving viewers to bear the purchase risk.

citations.quote: EARN A FREE $25 GIFT CARD WITH BABY PURCHASE (Starting 9/27)
Starting tomorrow, 9/27
FREE $25 Gift Card when you purchase $100 worth
check out all of the great coupons that you can stack to sweeten things even further

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats each signal in isolation. The relevant presentation combines a 'free' reward, a near-term start date, a spending threshold, coupon stacking, and an external destination. Those features make the viewer-facing message more than neutral information about prices. The description supplies an attractive headline and a link, but does not show terms resolving eligibility, exclusions, or actual delivery of the reward.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are ordinary promotion signals, not evidence of a scam mechanism. The time reference identifies when the advertised promotion starts, and the purchase threshold identifies the condition for the gift card. The description explicitly presents coupons as savings that can be stacked, while the link points to a deal article rather than requesting credentials or a transfer. Missing proof of later fulfillment cannot convert a documented retail offer into deception.

citations.quote: Starting tomorrow, 9/27, Target will be offering up a FREE $25 Gift Card
PLUS, find deals, coupons, and more on my site -- http://hip2save.com/

opening.argument: Although the material can be read as shopping advice, its function is promotional: it highlights a reward, directs viewers to a specific external page, and advertises the publisher's broader deal ecosystem. The description tells viewers to watch, click, and use coupons to make the offer more attractive, while the title foregrounds earning a gift card. That coordinated framing steers participation in a purchase-and-click funnel. The ordinary-store setting does not by itself prove that every advertised benefit will materialize.

****FOLLOW ME****
EARN A FREE $25 GIFT CARD WITH BABY PURCHASE (Starting 9/27)

rebuttal.rebuttal: The issue is not whether baby products are ordinary merchandise; it is how the content uses that setting. The title leads with earning money-equivalent value, the description instructs viewers to click, and it promotes the publisher's site and social accounts. Those are participation-oriented calls to action, not detached reporting. The defense's description of the merchandise therefore leaves the central promotional funnel unaddressed.

citations.quote: EARN A FREE $25 GIFT CARD WITH BABY PURCHASE (Starting 9/27)
Be sure to watch the video and click the link below
PLUS, find deals, coupons, and more on my site

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The calls to action remain consistent with a deal publisher sharing a retail promotion: viewers are directed to coupons and a deal page, not asked to send money, install software, or surrender sensitive information. The title's reward is expressly tied to a baby purchase, and the description names the products and threshold. Promotional tone alone does not show that the conditional store benefit is fraudulent.
